# routeros_system_watchdog (Resource)


## Example Usage
```terraform
resource "routeros_system_watchdog" "watchdog" {
  auto_send_supout      = true
  automatic_supout      = true
  ping_start_after_boot = "10s"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `___id___` (Number) <em>Resource ID type (.id / name). This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.</em>
- `___path___` (String) <em>Resource path for CRUD operations. This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.</em>
- `auto_send_supout` (Boolean) After the supout file is automatically generated, it can be sent by e-mail to the address configured in `send_email_to`.
- `automatic_supout` (Boolean) When a software failure happens, a file named `autosupout.rif` is generated automatically. The previous `autosupout.rif` file is renamed to `autosupout.old.rif`.
- `ping_start_after_boot` (String) Specifies how long the system waits after boot before it starts to reach the `watch_address` (known as `no-ping-delay` in older RouterOS versions).
- `ping_timeout` (String) Specifies the time interval in which the device will be pinged 6 times (after `ping_start_after_boot`).
- `send_email_from` (String) The e-mail address the supout file is sent from. If not set, the value from `/tool/e-mail` is used.
- `send_email_to` (String) The e-mail address to send the supout file to.
- `send_smtp_server` (String) The SMTP server used to send the supout file. If not set, the value from `/tool/e-mail` is used.
- `watch_address` (String) The system will reboot in case 6 sequential pings to the given IP address fail. `none` disables the ping watchdog.
- `watchdog_timer` (Boolean) Whether to reboot the device if the system is unresponsive for a minute.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

## Import
Import is supported using the following syntax:
```shell
#The ID can be found via API or the terminal
#The command for the terminal is -> :put [/system/watchdog get [print show-ids]]
terraform import routeros_system_watchdog.watchdog "*1"
```
